summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 12.6% to Rs 3,601 million, but EBITDA fell to Rs 410 million and margin to 11.4% from 14.4%.
summary.overview: Nath Bio-Genes reported H1 FY27 revenue up about 12.6% year on year to Rs 3,601 million, while EBITDA declined to Rs 410 million from Rs 461 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to extra trade schemes and incentives passed to distributors (about Rs 5 crore in the quarter) to protect the top line, plus a crop mix shift away from cotton. Working capital worsened: trade receivables rose to Rs 2,644 million from Rs 838 million at March 2026, and operating cash flow was negative for the half, while inventory eased to Rs 4,062 million from Rs 4,446 million. Management expects margins to recover by year-end, helped by the rabi season, but gave no quantified timeline.

segments.name: Paddy
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at about 37% of overall sales, supported by favourable rainfall in northern markets; hybrids Dada Gold, Dada Gold Cold and Gurtana cited as performing well.

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: About 26% of sales; volumes about 1.06 million packets, down 2.29% YoY on weather and weaker demand in some key markets. Flagship brands Sanket, Jumbo and Rana. Cotton seed inventory is elevated after heavy hybrid production; management is rationalising output.

segments.name: Bajra (pearl millet)
segments.commentary: About 13% of sales; management cited uplift over the last two to three years and two new hybrids entering volume building.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: About 6% of sales; management said maize gave good uplift this year and expects corn acreage to grow about 20% next year.

segments.name: International (Uzbekistan JV, Central Asia Ltd)
segments.commentary: About 90% owned JV; Rs 9 crore of sales consolidated in H1 per the call, with Rs 15 crore cited for March quarter. Still in loss-absorbing phase; no EBITDA guidance given. Exports are minimal, at Rs 5-10 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margin to recover by end of the year, helped by rabi crops, but gave no quantified target.
Management says trade schemes should decline to about 2.6-2.7% of sales next year from the elevated level this year.

Management is targeting a 14% net margin on a longer-term basis; it said a Rs 100 crore net profit would require about Rs 750 crore of revenue, while also calling 20% margins unrealistic for the sector.
Cotton seed demand expected to grow 20-30% next year, per management, on higher commercial prices (Rs 9,500-10,500 per quintal vs about Rs 7,500 last year).
Corn acreage expected to grow at least 20% in the next season.
Uzbekistan: first soft launch of Bt-GT cotton planned for 2028; no sales guidance given.
Management aims to reduce inventory and receivables and expects working capital to improve gradually.
capex_capacity: Cotton hybrid seed production efficiency improved over recent years, allowing volume build-up in previously difficult hybrids.
Excess cotton seed inventory to be liquidated over the next year after production rationalisation.
Uzbekistan JV signed agreement with the government to convert local cotton varieties to Bt-GT; soft launch targeted for 2028.
No specific capex or capacity figures were given on the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the H1 margin decline reflected extra trade schemes and margin passed to the trade to protect the top line, about Rs 5 crore additional in the quarter.
Illegal Bt cotton seed (unapproved) estimated at 20-25% of total cotton sales, mainly in Gujarat and Maharashtra; no company-level data available.
Government minimum support price for cotton for 2026-27 rose about 7%; commodity prices were cited as up 30-40% YoY.
Management stated competition is manageable if products perform, and cotton volume decline was attributed mainly to monsoon effects.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gap between revenue growth and the fall in profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it passed more margin to the trade through schemes to protect the top line, adding about Rs 5 crore in the quarter; it expects profit to follow once top line is secure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for EBITDA margin recovery from 11.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; management expects recovery by year-end, supported by rabi crops, and said margins move both ways.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company protecting share against illegal Bt cotton sellers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management relies on product performance and says government enforcement has been weak; it estimates illegal seed sales at 20-25% of cotton sales and is lobbying authorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cotton volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects cotton seed demand to grow 20-30% next year due to higher commercial prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher working capital borrowing to fund stock build-up raised interest by about Rs 3.5-4 crore; average cost of funds is about 9%, not higher rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uzbekistan outlook and expected margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin or sales guidance; it said the JV is still in an early loss-absorbing phase and that no Uzbekistan cash has been sent in the last two years.

risks_watch: Receivables rose to Rs 2,644 million from Rs 838 million in March 2026 and operating cash flow was negative; collections need monitoring.
Elevated cotton seed inventory and possible write-down risk if sales stay below plan.
Margin pressure from trade schemes; management says schemes may fall next year but gave no firm number.
Rising borrowing and interest costs due to working capital needs.
Illegal Bt cotton seed competition, estimated at 20-25% of cotton sales.
Uzbekistan JV remains loss-making with no clear breakeven and regulatory/land price risks.
Call transcript quality was poor; several figures (tax, interest, Uzbekistan sales) should be verified against filings.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term story but defensive on profitability, repeatedly saying top-line protection comes first and margins will follow. It was evasive on Uzbekistan margins and on timelines for the Rs 100 crore profit target. Tone on working capital was cautious.
key_quotes: Please understand that if the top line is maintained, the bottom line will always follow.
But if we lose the top line, we tend to lose the bottom line in any case.
So nobody will be able to put a time frame as to whether we will reach 100 crores of bottom line in 6 months 1 year 6 years 60 years.
I'm only looking at a 14 percent net margin which I think is achievable easily.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity additions, plants or lines were discussed; the only related item is excess cotton seed inventory being liquidated over the next year.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Receivables and inventory unwind
rows.why: Management aims to cut inventory (Rs 4,062m at Sep 2026 vs Rs 4,446m in March) and receivables (Rs 2,644m vs Rs 838m), but gave no quantified target and said working capital will improve only gradually.

rows.label: Trade scheme reduction
rows.why: Management says trade schemes should fall to about 2.6-2.7% of sales next year from the elevated level this year, which would support margins, though no firm number was given for the current year.

rows.label: Uzbekistan JV Bt-GT soft launch
